hits.draft_en:
Greg Isenberg listed 39 'obvious' startup ideas for the agent economy. 472k views and 10.1k bookmarks, about twice as many bookmarks as likes.

Almost all of them follow one template: take a boring, trusted product and rebuild it for agents.

Okta for agents (what each agent may touch). FICO for agents (a trust score before it can spend). Datadog for agents (every step it took). Geico for agents (insurance for expensive mistakes).

The useful filter: pick the one where you already know the buyer and the failure that costs them money.

hits.name: @levelsio
hits.text:
Finally learnt how to make 🍿 popcorn in a pan

I wanted to stop using those microwave popcorn bags

Microwave popcorn bags used to have a PFAS bag lining but that got banned in EU and US, but they're still not great. They use cheap palm oil (highly saturated fat) and synthetic butter flavoring (2,3-pentanedione a chemical twin of diacetyl that was used before and banned)

1) put a kinda tall pan, like a sauce pan, on medium to high heat (I use 12/14 on electric stove)
2) then make the pan very hot first like the sides have to feel hot too
3) then spray the pan inside with extra virgin olive oil (maybe you can use butter too? I will try next time)
4) then cover the pan with corn, it shouldn't stack, just level
5) keep pan open and wait until one corn pops
6) once it pops, put the lid fully on and start moving it back and forth kinda shaking, so the corns don't burn
7) then it takes about same as microwave popcorn, like 3-4mins, then once it stops popping every few seconds stop it
8) then add salt and put in a bowl

That gets you healthy popcorn with just olive oil and salt!

I'm not sure about adding salt before or after btw, I'll try, one problem adding it after is you sometimes breathe in the salt when eating cause it doesn't stick so well to the popcorn

hits.name: Hassan
hits.text:
How I build apps these days:

1. Record a 1-5 minute prompt with @WisprFlow The more detail, the better.
2. Add visual inspo so the agent knows what I have in mind (screenshots or Inspo MCP).
3. Use @mattpocockuk's grill-me skill to have the agent ask clarifying questions.
4. Get back a v1, then send a list of feedback, feature requests, and design tweaks (via another voice recording usually).
5. For each new feature, ask for a quick screen recording to verify it works before merging the PR.
6. Keep iterating until I'm happy, then post it on @X or throw it away.

For my harness, I use a mix of Claude Code with Opus 5.5 (high) and OpenCode with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash / GLM 5.3.

I also give my agents some CLIs & skills:

• Vercel + GitHub CLIs so they can push code and deploy apps.
• Together skills so they can use chat, image, & voice models from Together
• Design/animation skills so they have guidance on spacing & interactions
hits.hook: How I build apps these days:  1. Record a 1-5 minute prompt with @WisprFlow The more detail, the better. 2. Add visual i
hits.draft_en:
Hassan's app building loop, 40k views and 1.1k bookmarks:

1. Record a 1-5 minute voice prompt. More detail is better.
2. Add visual inspiration (screenshots or an MCP).
3. Use Matt Pocock's grill-me skill so the agent asks clarifying questions first.
4. Get a v1, then send voice feedback.
5. For every new feature, ask the agent for a screen recording before merging.
6. Keep iterating, then ship it or throw it away.

Step 5 is the one most people skip.

outsiders.name: OpenAI
outsiders.text:
Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live internet access for all frontier models during training and built an offline world for them to use instead—a cached version of the web where they can still learn to browse, search, and use applications.

On September 20, after a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to find a way outside of this offline world, we paused frontier training to strengthen containment further. We assembled teams of agents, powered by our most cyber-capable models, and tasked them with finding weaknesses in our research environments.

While they found no route to the internet they could easily exploit while concealing their activity from our monitors, they did find zero-day vulnerabilities, virtual machine escapes, and hardware side-channels for communication between agents. We used their discoveries to further strengthen our defenses and contribute fixes to open-source software.

After strengthening our containment architecture, we resumed our frontier RL training and inference on October 1. We’ve reserved substantial compute for continuous red-teaming, and made high-compute red-teaming part of the safety cases we use to decide whether frontier training and evaluation can proceed securely.

https://t.co/EmEZsFRMcF

BREAKING: OpenAI says it found a critical flaw in Brotli, a widely used compression library built into software like Node.js, Bun and Envoy.

The bug could let an attacker take over a system just by sending it malicious compressed data, with no login needed. That works both ways: a hacker could hijack an unpatched server, or a malicious server could hijack an unpatched user’s device.

outsiders.name: Cyber Security News
outsiders.text:
‼️  Tailscale SSH Flaws Could Let Hackers Gain Root Access Across Servers 

Details: https://t.co/BLfO3GLSaZ

A new security report warns that Tailscale SSH has flaws that could let a hacker move from one compromised device to root access on other servers. Tailscale SSH lets approved devices log in to each other over a private network. The report lists 11 findings in five groups.

They cover Tailscale’s SSH server, its serve and app connector features, the DERP relay client, and headscale, an open-source server that manages Tailscale networks.

The researcher tested Tailscale 1.104.2 and headscale 0.29.5 between October 22 and October 24, 2026. The most serious group involves Tailscale SSH. Its SSH server runs inside tailscaled, a background program with full root privileges on the machine.

#cybersecuritynews

outsiders.name: Semgrep
outsiders.text:
If you're looking at an updated Node.js, and calling CVE-2026-111497 done? We have some bad news: We likely don't even know the true scale of "Node2Shell" yet.

Node patched CVE-2026-111497 on Oct 21. But the CVE wasn't in Node, it was in Brotli. So our researchers Diptendu Kar and Kurt Boberg went looking for every other package that bundles the same vulnerable Brotli decoder. Here's what we found

433 package entries across 12 ecosystems not great but the absolute worse part: Many of them don't even have fixes available yet. Now are they all reachable and exploitable? Probably not, we're finding out. But the important part: Node isn't the only affected runtime or package, not even close.

We're working through the list to manually verify each one but so far we're looking at a 71% no fix yet rate, of the fixes most are still in alpha/early releases.

The problem is most implementations aren't even called "brotli." The decoder is compiled into other runtimes like Chromium. 38 entries bundle Brotli older than 1.0.3. Some of those copies date to 2016, and of course are vulnerable to more than just this CVE. And there's no easy well to tell if you're affected.

For example, 19 are WebAssembly builds, where memory corruption exists, but stays inside the sandbox. Some require explicit configurations to enable Brotli compression and they aren't on by default. But it's not obvious unless you are looking for it and testing for it. We're going to keep validating (and producing rules), but it's going to be a rough weekend for incident responders.

virals.angle: Add a security week to your month
virals.draft_en:
Pieter spent a day typing one prompt into Claude Code on every server he runs: 'Do a full security audit of this website and server.'

Marc Lou spent 48 hours rotating passwords, adding 2FA everywhere and pointing agents at his codebases.

A monthly security week, in four steps:
1. Run an audit prompt on each server and repo
2. Turn on automatic security updates
3. Isolate machines so one hacked box can't reach the rest
4. Rotate keys and add 2FA or a hardware key

Then read the report yourself. Don't just trust the green checkmarks.

virals.angle: Read the advisory before you panic
virals.draft_en:
A report on Tailscale SSH flaws hit 623k views this weekend: 11 findings, one path from a compromised device to root on other servers.

A researcher replied that none of the 11 touch a default install.

Both can be true. What to do:
1. Check whether you turned on Tailscale SSH, Serve or App Connectors
2. Update to the latest version
3. Restrict which devices can reach which with access policies

Panic posts travel faster than the fix. Read the actual advisory.

virals.draft_en:
Node patched the Brotli bug on Oct 21. Semgrep then went looking for everything else that bundles the same decoder: 433 package entries across 12 ecosystems, and so far about 71% have no fix yet, by their count.

Bun shipped fixes in 1.4.4. Cloudflare's CEO: 'Get used to lots of patching.'

This week:
1. Update your runtime (Node, Bun)
2. Rebuild anything you compiled with the old version
3. Check your Docker images and CI for pinned old versions

virals.angle: Talk to your agent, then make it prove it
virals.draft_en:
The most saved build workflow this weekend (Hassan, 1.1k bookmarks):

1. Record a 1-5 minute voice prompt
2. Add screenshots of what you want
3. Have the agent ask you clarifying questions first
4. Send feedback by voice
5. For every feature, ask for a screen recording before you merge

Matt Pocock's add-on: split risky changes into an easy-to-revert PR plus a small follow-up.

Talking is faster than typing. A recording is proof the feature works.

virals.angle: The agent economy needs boring tools
virals.draft_en:
Greg Isenberg's 39 startup ideas got 10.1k bookmarks. Almost every one is a boring, trusted product rebuilt for agents:

- Okta for agents: what each agent may touch
- FICO for agents: a trust score before it spends
- Datadog for agents: every step it took
- Geico for agents: insurance for expensive mistakes

The same weekend, Grok Bot started making phone calls for people, and Anthropic filed its S-1.

Agents are taking actions with money. Someone has to build the guardrails.

virals_narrative: Window Oct 23 ~11:15 CT (after Friday's digest) through Oct 26 ~11:20 CT, so Friday afternoon, the weekend and Monday morning. The security story kept rolling and got more practical. drafts.angle: Add a security week to your month
drafts.draft_en:
Pieter spent a day typing one prompt into Claude Code on every server he runs: 'Do a full security audit of this website and server.'

Marc Lou spent 48 hours rotating passwords, adding 2FA everywhere and pointing agents at his codebases.

A monthly security week, in four steps:
1. Run an audit prompt on each server and repo
2. Turn on automatic security updates
3. Isolate machines so one hacked box can't reach the rest
4. Rotate keys and add 2FA or a hardware key

Then read the report yourself. Don't just trust the green checkmarks.

drafts.angle: Read the advisory before you panic
drafts.draft_en:
A report on Tailscale SSH flaws hit 623k views this weekend: 11 findings, one path from a compromised device to root on other servers.

A researcher replied that none of the 11 touch a default install.

Both can be true. What to do:
1. Check whether you turned on Tailscale SSH, Serve or App Connectors
2. Update to the latest version
3. Restrict which devices can reach which with access policies

Panic posts travel faster than the fix. Read the actual advisory.
drafts.inspired_by: @The_Cyber_News Tailscale SSH flaws (623k) + @theonejvo 'none touch a default install' (23k) + @levelsio 'now it's Tailscale's turn' (114k)
drafts.video_tip: 10s: a red headline zooming in, then a checklist calmly ticking off, caption check what you enabled.

drafts.angle: The bug is inside something you didn't install
drafts.draft_en:
Node patched the Brotli bug on Oct 21. Semgrep then went looking for everything else that bundles the same decoder: 433 package entries across 12 ecosystems, and so far about 71% have no fix yet, by their count.

Bun shipped fixes in 1.4.4. Cloudflare's CEO: 'Get used to lots of patching.'

This week:
1. Update your runtime (Node, Bun)
2. Rebuild anything you compiled with the old version
3. Check your Docker images and CI for pinned old versions

drafts.angle: Talk to your agent, then make it prove it
drafts.draft_en:
The most saved build workflow this weekend (Hassan, 1.1k bookmarks):

1. Record a 1-5 minute voice prompt
2. Add screenshots of what you want
3. Have the agent ask you clarifying questions first
4. Send feedback by voice
5. For every feature, ask for a screen recording before you merge

Matt Pocock's add-on: split risky changes into an easy-to-revert PR plus a small follow-up.

Talking is faster than typing. A recording is proof the feature works.

drafts.angle: The agent economy needs boring tools
drafts.draft_en:
Greg Isenberg's 39 startup ideas got 10.1k bookmarks. Almost every one is a boring, trusted product rebuilt for agents:

- Okta for agents: what each agent may touch
- FICO for agents: a trust score before it spends
- Datadog for agents: every step it took
- Geico for agents: insurance for expensive mistakes

The same weekend, Grok Bot started making phone calls for people, and Anthropic filed its S-1.

Agents are taking actions with money. Someone has to build the guardrails.
